objective: 0.3.0 pi 9/10: Document and ship the install path for the Pi integration, so a user can install the pinned package and Pi prerequisites and find the usage in the docs.
requirements: Maintainer (verbatim): "please add intents for the next 0.3.0 release where I will implement the pi extension integration"; the maintainer implements 0.3.0, so these Intents record the work and carry no Assignments until the maintainer starts it.
Maintainer (verbatim): "in the docs/pi/ it's supposed to use already existent extensions for required functionality" and "the first provider to implement will be kimi for coding global".

Release model: work lands on release/0.3.0/integration cut from main, as one release/0.3.0/<type>/<change> branch and one PR per change; the first PR of the release carries the version bump made with mise run bump:minor.
Done means mise run verify passes with the generated output in sync (mise run build) and CI green on every required check, including the windows job.

The documented Pi install is Node.js 22.19 or newer plus the official installer or npm install -g --ignore-scripts @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@<pinned>; the HolyAgent package is installed with pi install npm:...@x.y.z (or a git or local source) so the pin is explicit; Bun is documented as needed by the HolyAgent CLI, not as a Pi install route.

docs/components.md no longer says there is no Pi integration, and docs/usage.md, docs/development.md (layout and generated paths) and docs/pi/README.md describe the new package and how to start the root.
README.md keeps exactly its six sections in order; any Pi mention there is a link into docs/.

Open: the distribution channel for the Pi package; the repository publishes GitHub releases and tags, has no npm publishing, and the research names pi install sources npm:, git:, https and local path.
Open: whether the installers or holyagent setup and doctor install or check Pi; the Windows installer refuses Node older than 22.13 while Pi needs 22.19.
Open: the rule for moving the pinned Pi version, given weekly Pi releases and the deps:update flow.
Open: whether Bun is a supported way to install or run Pi; the research finds it undocumented and the Pi CLI shebang targets Node.
Maintainer (verbatim): "the pi extension and integration will use a config.json that will set options, functionality, the provider, which will enable/disable its deps, etc".

The config.json from Intent 0.3.0 pi 4/10 selects this: the docs describe every config.json option with its default, and installing the package installs only the dependencies the default config.json enables.
